cues.en: After the death of Socrates
cues.zh: 苏格拉底死后

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 以及

cues.en: the breakup of Greek culture
cues.zh: 希腊文化的崩解

cues.en: that resulted from the Peloponnesian War,
cues.zh: 那源于伯罗奔尼撒战争，

cues.en: Socratic philosophy went into a decline
cues.zh: 苏格拉底哲学走向衰落

cues.en: and fragmented
cues.zh: 并碎裂

cues.en: into several pieces,
cues.zh: 成几个部分，

cues.en: and the fragments of Socratic philosophy make up the body of Hellenistic philosophy. What I mean by Hellenistic philosophy
cues.zh: 而苏格拉底哲学的碎片构成了希腊化哲学的主体。我说的希腊化哲学

cues.en: is the subsequent developments
cues.zh: 是指希腊哲学的后续发展，

cues.en: of Greek philosophy, which take their cue from the Socratic approach to philosophy,
cues.zh: 它们从苏格拉底式的哲学方法中获得启发，

cues.en: yet they don't have all the component parts of Socratic philosophy.
cues.zh: 但并不具备苏格拉底哲学的全部组成部分。

cues.en: They usually lack lack the wit. They almost always lack the poetry. Occasionally, they absorb some of the ethical doctrines or epistemological doctrines, but the ones who come after Socrates
cues.zh: 它们通常缺少机智。几乎总是缺少诗意。偶尔，它们吸收一些伦理学说或认识论学说，但苏格拉底之后的那些人

cues.en: never really live up to the Socratic ideal.
cues.zh: 从未真正达到苏格拉底的理想。

cues.en: The three main fragments that Socratic philosophy breaks into are called Stoicism,
cues.zh: 苏格拉底哲学碎裂成的三个主要部分被称为斯多葛主义、

cues.en: Epicureanism,
cues.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁主义

cues.en: and Skepticism.
cues.zh: 和怀疑主义。

cues.en: And these are the most important Hellenistic outgrowths
cues.zh: 这些是苏格拉底哲学最重要的希腊化衍生物

cues.en: from Socratic philosophy.
And since Rome,
cues.zh: 而由于罗马，

cues.en: the Roman Empire in particular, is the political entity which ultimately
cues.zh: 尤其是罗马帝国，是最终

cues.en: dominates the Mediterranean Basin and absorbs and inherits the tradition of Greek philosophy,
cues.zh: 主宰地中海盆地并吸收和继承希腊哲学传统的政治实体，

cues.en: most of the
cues.zh: 大多数

cues.en: Hellenistic branches of philosophy are developed
cues.zh: 希腊化哲学分支的发展

cues.en: in connection or with reference to either politically
cues.zh: 都与罗马文化在政治上

cues.en: or intellectually
cues.zh: 或思想上

cues.en: with Roman culture.
cues.zh: 相关联或参照。

cues.en: And the first of these developments is hedonism or epicureanism,
cues.zh: 这些发展中的第一个是享乐主义或伊壁鸠鲁主义，

cues.en: named after a guy named Epicurus.
cues.zh: 以一位名叫伊壁鸠鲁的人命名。

cues.en: And what epicureanism says is that pleasure is the only good,
cues.zh: 伊壁鸠鲁主义认为，快乐是唯一的善，

cues.en: and that the happy man is the one that has a great many pleasures, but no corresponding pains.
cues.zh: 而幸福的人就是拥有许多快乐、却没有相应痛苦的人。

cues.en: And there is potentially a way of deriving that from Socratic philosophy.
cues.zh: 而且有可能从苏格拉底哲学中推导出这一点。

cues.en: If you would take the idea of Socratic prudence, the man who drinks a little bit in order to get a certain degree of pleasure, but then not so much as he will cause himself a hangover or cause himself some corresponding pain, he's being prudently Socratic,
cues.zh: 如果你采用苏格拉底式审慎的理念——那个人喝一点酒以获得某种程度的快乐，但不会喝到让自己宿醉或给自己造成相应痛苦的程度，他就是在审慎地践行苏格拉底之道，

cues.en: picking and choosing his pleasures
cues.zh: 挑选和选择自己的快乐，

cues.en: in such a way that he does not generate any corresponding pains. You
cues.zh: 以不产生任何相应痛苦的方式。你

cues.en: can see possibly how people who were not entirely developed to the, or who were not entirely committed to the Socratic conception of the soul and of virtue might want to derive that sort of justification for the pursuit of pleasure from the Socratic dialogues.
cues.zh: 或许能看出，那些尚未完全发展到、或尚未完全认同苏格拉底关于灵魂与德性之构想的人，为何可能想从苏格拉底对话录中为追求快乐推导出那种正当性。

cues.en: A second alternative,
cues.zh: 第二种替代方案，

cues.en: again a minor alternative
cues.zh: 同样是苏格拉底哲学的一个次要替代

cues.en: fragment of Socratic philosophy, called skepticism.
cues.zh: 片段，叫做怀疑主义。

cues.en: Socrates, throughout most of the dialogues, I would emphasize
cues.zh: 苏格拉底在大多数对话录中——我要强调

cues.en: the word most rather than all, says that he doesn't know anything. Part of the Socratic irony is this posture
cues.zh: 是“大多数”而非“全部”——都说自己一无所知。苏格拉底式反讽的一部分就是这种姿态：

cues.en: of acting as if he's really an ignorant man, when in fact he is wise,
cues.zh: 表现得好像自己真是个无知之人，而实际上他是智慧的，

cues.en: in saying that he knows nothing, and thus never trying to teach people by directly making declarative sentences. For the most part, Socrates teaches by question and answer. Socrates helps people to articulate
cues.zh: 他说自己什么都不知道，因此从不试图通过直接做出陈述句来教导别人。大多数时候，苏格拉底通过问答来教学。苏格拉底帮助人们阐明

cues.en: and to realize what's already buried within their soul. When Socrates does that, when he's in that skeptical mode, he says, I myself know nothing. All I do is inquire into things. I'm the eternal equieter. I'm the patron saint of rational inquiry.
cues.zh: 并意识到已经埋藏在他们灵魂中的东西。当苏格拉底这样做、当他处于那种怀疑模式时，他说，我自己一无所知。我所做的只是探究事物。我是永恒的质疑者。我是理性探究的守护圣人。

cues.en: And it's possible to see, particularly within the context of the Roman Empire,
cues.zh: 尤其在罗马帝国的背景下，我们可以看出，

cues.en: how skepticism
cues.zh: 怀疑主义是如何

cues.en: might develop from that Socratic stance of knowing nothing. Remember that the Roman Empire is a heterogeneous mix of peoples and cultures and religions and philosophical positions.
cues.zh: 从苏格拉底那种“自知无知”的立场演变而来的。要记住，罗马帝国是一个融合了不同民族、文化、宗教和哲学立场的多元大熔炉。

cues.en: And after being forced to encounter
cues.zh: 在被迫面对了

cues.en: one cosmogonic myth after another, one theory of religion after another, one theory of morals after another, sophisticated
cues.zh: 一个又一个创世神话、宗教理论和道德学说之后，见多识广的

cues.en: Romans, sophisticated Hellenistic thinkers might well come to the conclusion that Lucian the skeptic did, which is that no one really knows the right path, no one even knows if there is a right path. The best we can do is say that the pretensions made by the various schools of philosophy are just that, pretensions.
cues.zh: 罗马人和希腊化思想家们，很可能得出与怀疑论者 Lucian 相同的结论：没人真正知道正确的道路，甚至没人知道究竟存不存在正确的道路。我们充其量只能说，各个哲学流派的宣称不过是在自命不凡。

cues.en: Skepticism,
cues.zh: 怀疑主义

cues.en: while it may be rather negative, is at least right. We can be certain about what we do not know.
cues.zh: 尽管可能相当消极，但至少它是对的。我们能够确切知道自己不知道什么。

cues.en: Alright? And it's possible to see how someone, especially someone that was terribly frustrated with the attempt to obtain final, absolute knowledge, might resort to skepticism as a kind of easy way out, a way of avoiding the burden of Socratic inquiry.
cues.zh: 明白了吧？我们也不难理解，一个人（尤其是那些因苦求终极、绝对知识而备受挫折的人）为什么会把怀疑主义当作一种轻松的退路，以此来逃避苏格拉底式探究的沉重负担。

cues.en: The third and most important
cues.zh: 第三个、也是最重要的

cues.en: development in Hellenistic philosophy is called Stoicism.
cues.zh: 希腊化哲学发展，被称为斯多葛主义。

cues.en: And Stoicism is probably the greatest and most interesting achievement of
cues.zh: 斯多葛主义大概是

cues.en: Hellenistic
cues.zh: 希腊化

cues.en: philosophers.
cues.zh: 哲学家们最伟大、最有趣的成就。

cues.en: And while it never achieves the poetic and intellectual grandeur of the Socratic synthesis,
cues.zh: 尽管它从未达到苏格拉底综合体、

cues.en: of the Platonic overarching system,
cues.zh: 或是柏拉图宏大体系那种诗意与理智的崇高境界，

cues.en: makes statements about the entire human condition,
cues.zh: 亦未对整个人类生存境况做出宏观论断，

cues.en: Stoicism is, in fact, a noble philosophy,
cues.zh: 但斯多葛主义实际上是一种崇高的哲学，

cues.en: an excellent philosophy for silver men, for those spirited men in the Republic who are going to be our guardians. It's an excellent philosophy for military men. It's an excellent philosophy for people that are going to be practical politicians if they intend to be virtuous, if they intend to pursue the public good.
cues.zh: 非常适合“白银阶层”，也就是《理想国》中那些成为守卫者的血气方刚之人。它非常适合军人。对于那些想要立德行善、追求公共利益的务实政治家来说，也是一门极佳的哲学。

cues.en: Stoicism
cues.zh: 斯多葛主义

cues.en: is characterized
cues.zh: 其核心特征在于

cues.en: by a rejection of pleasure as the standard of human happiness and human felicity.
cues.zh: 否定将享乐作为衡量人类幸福的标准。

cues.en: Stoicism takes the position that the wise man, the good man, the philosopher,
cues.zh: 斯多葛主义认为，智者、善者与哲学家，

cues.en: is a man who lives in accordance with nature.
cues.zh: 是顺应自然而活的人。

cues.en: He fears only
cues.zh: 他唯一恐惧的，

cues.en: abdicating his moral responsibility.
cues.zh: 是放弃自己的道德责任。

cues.en: He is not afraid of pain, he is not afraid of death, he is not afraid of poverty, he is not afraid of any of the vicissitudes of the human condition. He fears only that he should let himself down and that he should be less than a complete human being.
cues.zh: 他不惧痛苦，不惧死亡，不惧贫困，也不惧人世间的任何沧桑变故。他只担心辜负自己，担心自己没能成为一个完整的人。

cues.en: According to the Stoics, and there are a number of Stoics, two or three or four or five that actually developed the doctrine, but all the doctrines are quite similar,
cues.zh: 按照斯多葛学派的说法——虽然有几位代表人物发展了这套学说，但他们的思想都大同小异——

cues.en: the only matter of concern to a wise and philosophic individual
cues.zh: 真正值得有智慧、有哲学修养的人关心的，

cues.en: is the things completely under your control.
cues.zh: 只有完全处于你掌控之中的事物。

cues.en: You can't control the movements of the sun and the planets.
cues.zh: 你无法控制太阳与行星的运转。

cues.en: You can't control whether a leaky ship sinks or makes it to port.
cues.zh: 你无法控制一艘漏水的船是会沉没还是能安全靠岸。

cues.en: You can't control the weather. You can't control other people. You can't control the society around you. There's only one thing, and one thing only, that you are in control of, and that is you. Your will,
cues.zh: 你无法控制天气，无法控制他人，也无法控制周遭的社会。你真正能掌控的只有一件事，且唯有这一件事，那就是你自己。你的意志、

cues.en: your intentions, yourself.
cues.zh: 你的意图，以及你自己。

cues.en: In other words, the wise man, the truly philosophical man, is the man who is entirely in control of his own soul,
cues.zh: 换句话说，智者，即真正具有哲学精神的人，是一个能够完全掌控自己灵魂的人，

cues.en: who takes utter and complete moral responsibility for his actions, and is indifferent to everything else, not because he doesn't care about other people, not because he doesn't care about the felicity of the entire human species,
cues.zh: 他对自己的行为承担绝对且完全的道德责任，并对其余一切泰然处之；这并不是因为他不关心他人，也不是不关心全人类的福祉，

cues.en: but because it's not under his control. There's no use wondering or worrying
cues.zh: 而是因为那些并不在他掌控之中。去猜测或担忧

cues.en: about what tomorrow will bring, since tomorrow isn't under your control. Do what's right today, and let tomorrow take care of itself.
cues.zh: 明天会发生什么毫无意义，因为明天不在你的掌控之中。今天做正确的事，明天顺其自然就好。

cues.en: The stoic philosopher is the man who has liberated himself from fear.
cues.zh: 斯多葛哲人，就是把自己从恐惧中解放出来的人。

cues.en: He's not afraid of death,
cues.zh: 他不怕死，

cues.en: he's not afraid of pain,
cues.zh: 他不怕痛苦，

cues.en: he's not afraid of other people's dismissal as a fool.
cues.zh: 他不怕别人把他当傻瓜而轻视他。

cues.en: The only thing he cares about is that he should meet his moral obligations.
cues.zh: 他唯一在乎的，是履行自己的道德义务。

cues.en: Ralph Waldo Emerson once said that
cues.zh: Ralph Waldo Emerson 曾说，

cues.en: greatness is the perception that virtue is enough.
cues.zh: 伟大就在于认识到美德已经足够。

cues.en: Just an elegant and beautiful line. And he might well have stolen that from one of the Stoics
cues.zh: 一句优雅又漂亮的话。他很可能还是从某位斯多葛派那里偷来的

cues.en: because all of the Stoics basically believed that. Virtue, moral virtue,
cues.zh: 因为所有斯多葛派基本都相信这一点。美德，道德美德，

cues.en: an organized soul which pursues rationally
cues.zh: 一个有条理的灵魂，能理性地追求

cues.en: the ends which are good for all human beings, that's the Stoic conception of virtue.
cues.zh: 对全人类都有益的目的——这就是斯多葛派的美德观。

cues.en: They finally understand their greatness consists in the fact that they perceive that virtue is enough.
cues.zh: 他们终于明白，自己的伟大在于认识到美德已经足够。

cues.en: We do not need wealth.
cues.zh: 我们不需要财富。

cues.en: We do not need sexual gratification.
cues.zh: 我们不需要性满足。

cues.en: We do not need life itself.
cues.zh: 我们不需要生命本身。

cues.en: If moral virtue tells us that we must die in the pursuit of some good end, the protection of our family, the protection of our home, the protection of the innocent.
cues.zh: 如果道德美德告诉我们，为了追求某个善的目的——保护家人、保护家园、保护无辜者——我们必须赴死。

cues.en: In the doing of right,
cues.zh: 在行正道时，

cues.en: nothing should be spared, not even our lives.
cues.zh: 不应吝惜任何东西，甚至我们的生命。

cues.en: The stoic wise man is a man who has trained his soul, trained his mind, so that he is not afraid
cues.zh: 斯多葛派的智者，是训练了自己的灵魂、训练了自己的心智，从而不再害怕

cues.en: of apparent evils. He's only afraid of real evil. He's afraid of losing control of his soul.
cues.zh: 表面的恶。他只害怕真正的恶。他害怕失去对自己灵魂的控制。

cues.en: He is afraid
cues.zh: 他害怕

cues.en: of being a slave to lust, to desire,
cues.zh: 沦为淫欲、欲望的奴隶，

cues.en: to emotion.
cues.zh: 沦为情绪的奴隶。

cues.en: The stoic man is the honorable philosopher,
cues.zh: 斯多葛派的人，是可敬的哲学家，

cues.en: the man who stands at his duty and is steadfast and serious minded.
cues.zh: 是坚守职责、坚定而严肃认真的人。

cues.en: In living according to nature,
cues.zh: 顺应自然而生活，

cues.en: what the stoic philosopher does is examine the nature of the human condition and the nature of the world around us. He discerns his position in nature, he discerns the kind of creature that he is, and he lives in such a way as not to disgrace himself, as not to be less than what he truly could be.
cues.zh: 斯多葛学派哲学家所做的，就是审视人类生存状态的本质以及我们周围世界的本质。他辨明自己在自然中的位置，辨明自己是何种生物，并以此种方式生活：不让自己蒙羞，不让自己辜负真正的潜能。

cues.en: He won't live the swinish life that we found with Aristophanes.
cues.zh: 他不会过着我们在阿里斯托芬作品里看到的那种猪猡般的生活。

cues.en: He wants to be, if not
cues.zh: 他渴望成为，即使成不了

cues.en: a god, certainly not less than human. He won't be an animal either. He will live up to the fullest potentials
cues.zh: 神，也绝不低于人类。他也不会沦为动物。他将活出

cues.en: that human being has to offer.
cues.zh: 人类所能提供的全部潜能。

cues.en: Now, among the Roman Stoics,
cues.zh: 在罗马斯多葛学派中，

cues.en: two are especially noteworthy.
cues.zh: 有两个人尤为值得一提。

cues.en: One is Epictetus,
cues.zh: 一个是爱比克泰德，

cues.en: and one is Marcus Aurelius.
cues.zh: 另一个是马可·奥勒留。

cues.en: And one of the wonderful ironies about the history of philosophy
cues.zh: 哲学史上有一个奇妙的讽刺，

cues.en: is that Epictetus was a slave and Marcus Aurelius was an emperor.
cues.zh: 那就是爱比克泰德曾是个奴隶，而马可·奥勒留是个皇帝。

cues.en: Philosophy is the great equalizer.
cues.zh: 哲学是伟大的拉平者。

cues.en: Both the slave and the emperor
cues.zh: 无论是奴隶还是皇帝，

cues.en: can equally well participate
cues.zh: 都可以同样地参与到

cues.en: in a philosophy that is accessible to all human beings as human beings. There is nothing less
cues.zh: 这门对所有人类都开放的哲学中。没有什么比哲学

cues.en: conscious of social status than philosophy.
cues.zh: 更无视社会地位了。

cues.en: A wise man, a man who is disciplined, in control of his motions,
cues.zh: 一个智者，一个自律、能控制自己情绪、

cues.en: and follows the way of nature, can be a good man no matter what his position in the social structure is. He is not responsible for the social structure, and it is not his problem. If the gods or nature or whatever is controlling the world makes you a slave, then be a good slave. If god or nature or whatever is controlling the world makes you an emperor, then be a good one. Your job is not to disgrace yourself and live up to the highest potentials of human being.
cues.zh: 遵循自然之道的人，无论在社会结构中处于什么位置，都能成为一个好人。他不对社会结构负责，那也不是他该操心的问题。如果神明、自然或任何控制世界的力量让你成为奴隶，那就做一个好奴隶。如果神明、自然或任何控制世界的力量让你成为皇帝，那就做一个好皇帝。你的职责是不要让自己蒙羞，并活出人类最高的潜能。

cues.en: The most interesting of the Stoics is Marcus Aurelius.
cues.zh: 斯多葛学派中最有趣的是马可·奥勒福。

cues.en: Lord Acton, the great English philosopher
cues.zh: 阿克顿勋爵，这位伟大的英国哲学家

cues.en: and historian, once said that power corrupts
cues.zh: 兼历史学家，曾说过权力会腐蚀人，

cues.en: and absolute power corrupts absolutely.
cues.zh: 而绝对权力会绝对地腐蚀人。

cues.en: And that's generally speaking true.
cues.zh: 这话一般来说是对的。

cues.en: The difficulty with that generalization is Marcus Aurelius.
cues.zh: 这个概括的难点就在于马可·奥勒福。

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius was an absolute ruler. He was a ruler of the Roman Empire. He was an emperor.
cues.zh: 马可·奥勒福是个绝对的统治者。他是罗马帝国的统治者。他是一位皇帝。

cues.en: He had absolute power of life and death over everyone in the known world. I don't mean everyone in the world as we know it today, but everyone in the world as as the Romans would have known it. They don't know about China or have a very attenuated conception of the Eskimos. For them, the world is the Mediterranean Basin, and Rome owns it. And Marcus Aurelius owns Rome, essentially. His word is law.
cues.zh: 对于当时已知世界中的所有人，他拥有生杀予夺的绝对权力。我指的不是今天我们所知的世界所有人，而是罗马人所理解的世界所有人。他们不知道中国，或者对爱斯基摩人只有非常模糊的概念。对他们而言，世界就是地中海盆地，而罗马拥有它。从本质上讲，马可·奥勒福拥有罗马。他的话就是法律。

cues.en: Now, for almost all the Roman emperors, they lived scandalous lives, and they disgraced themselves. They were much more concerned with indulging their sensual appetites,
cues.zh: 然而，几乎所有的罗马皇帝都过着声名狼藉的生活，自取其辱。他们更关心的是放纵感官欲望，

cues.en: satisfying their passions, flying into rages.
cues.zh: 满足激情，动辄大发雷霆。

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius is the standing exception to that, and the exception to Lord Acton's generalization.
cues.zh: 马可·奥勒福是个明显的例外，也是阿克顿勋爵那句断言的例外。

cues.en: In his case, power didn't corrupt.
cues.zh: 在他身上，权力并没有腐蚀他。

cues.en: Absolute power did not corrupt absolutely.
cues.zh: 绝对权力并没有绝对地腐蚀他。

cues.en: Instead, absolute power allowed us to see what the man underneath the body is really like. It allowed us to find out what Marcus Aurelius' soul is like. Imagine a man for whom all the restraints of law and custom and political order are taken away. He can have whatever he wants.
cues.zh: 相反，绝对权力让我们得以看清这个肉体凡胎之下的灵魂究竟是什么样。它让我们得以了解马可·奥勒福的灵魂。想象一下这样一个男人，法律、习俗和政治秩序的所有约束在他身上都不复存在。他想要什么就能有什么。

cues.en: If a man under those circumstances behaves well, you know something about the soul underneath, because no external constraint is making him do what he what he is doing. And Marcus Aurelius is the one example of an absolute ruler
cues.zh: 如果一个人在那种境况下还能行得正，你就能看清他内心的灵魂，因为没有任何外部约束在迫使他这么做。而 Marcus Aurelius 就是专制君主中绝无仅有的一个例子，

cues.en: who behaves himself in such a way as not to disgrace himself.
cues.zh: 他的所作所为从未让自己蒙羞。

cues.en: It's an amazing temptation. Imagine what it's like. Stop and put yourself in that place for a second. Marcus Aurelius takes the throne in one hundred sixty one AD, and he dies in one hundred eighty AD.
cues.zh: 那是极大的诱惑。想象一下那种感觉。停下来，设身处地想一秒钟。Marcus Aurelius 在公元 161 年登基，死于公元 180 年。

cues.en: Nineteen years
cues.zh: 整整十九年，

cues.en: controlling the entire world. He
cues.zh: 掌控着整个世界。他

cues.en: can have all the money in the world.
cues.zh: 可以拥有世上所有的财富。

cues.en: That's not an exaggeration. All the money in the world. If he wants it, he can just collect it all.
cues.zh: 这绝非夸张。全世界所有的财富。只要他想要，就能全部据为己有。

cues.en: He can have sex with anyone he wants, whenever he wants, under any circumstances.
cues.zh: 他可以在任何时间、任何场合，随心所欲地与任何人行鱼水之欢。

cues.en: If he wants to get drunk, he can have wine brought in by the boatload,
cues.zh: 如果他想买醉，美酒可以用一船又一船地运来，

cues.en: infinitely, forever. He can go on a drunk now and stay drunk for the next nineteen years until he dies.
cues.zh: 源源不断，直到永远。他现在就可以大醉一场，并在接下来的十九年里一直醉下去，直到死去。

cues.en: Imagine anything
cues.zh: 想象一下，

cues.en: that the bronze,
cues.zh: 那些最粗鄙的、

cues.en: desiring,
cues.zh: 充满欲望的、

cues.en: emotional, irrational parts of your souls want,
cues.zh: 情绪化且非理性的灵魂深处所渴望的一切，

cues.en: and now imagine that you can have it.
cues.zh: 然后再想象一下，这一切你都能唾手可得。

cues.en: Now, under those circumstances,
cues.zh: 现在，在那种境况下，

cues.en: imagine that you are forced to bear with this human condition for nineteen long years.
cues.zh: 想象你不得不作为凡人去承受这一切，长达整整十九年。

cues.en: Now ask yourself, and you didn't give a show of hands, but stop and think about it for a minute. How many of you would fail to disgrace yourselves?
cues.zh: 现在扪心自问——大家不用举手，但停下来思考一分钟。你们当中有几个人能做到不让自己蒙羞？

cues.en: To
cues.zh: 致

cues.en: tell you the truth, I don't think that I could meet the challenge. If
cues.zh: 说实话，我觉得我无法迎接这个挑战。如果

cues.en: you're honest about it, and you stop and think about what kind of a man it takes to bear up under those circumstances,
cues.zh: 你对此坦诚相待，然后停下来思考，在那种情况下承受这一切需要什么样的男子气概，

cues.en: I think you'll have to admit, or at least I'll have to admit, that he's a better man than I am, and that in this respect, over the centuries,
cues.zh: 我想你得承认，或者至少我得承认，他比我更优秀，而且在这方面，几个世纪以来，

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius serves as a standing reproach
cues.zh: Marcus Aurelius 犹如一座长存的警钟

cues.en: to our self indulgence,
cues.zh: 为了满足我们自身的纵容，

cues.en: a standing reproach to the idea that we are unable
cues.zh: 对我们无能为力这一观点的永恒谴责

cues.en: to deal with the circumstances of human life. If you can deal with temptation at that level,
cues.zh: 为了应付人类生活的种种境遇。如果你能在那个层面上抵御诱惑，

cues.en: I cannot imagine what is outside the human potential. And for the Stoics, we must remember that any virtue which is accessible to any human being is in principle accessible to all of us. We all have a rational nature, which allows us to control our feelings, control our behavior, control our
cues.zh: 我无法想象人类潜能的极限在哪里。对于斯多葛学派来说，我们必须记住，任何人类能够企及的美德，原则上我们所有人都能企及。我们都拥有理性的本性，它让我们能够控制自己的情绪、控制自己的行为、控制自己的

cues.en: connection to other people.
cues.zh: 与他人的连接。

cues.en: Compared to Marcus Aurelius, we have tiny little temptations.
cues.zh: 与马可·奥勒留相比，我们的诱惑微不足道。

cues.en: We're tempted to steal a little thing. We're tempted to cheat on our income taxes. We're tempted to cheat on our spouses. Marcus Aurelius has that sort of temptation
cues.zh:
我们总会忍不住去偷一点小东西。
@@
我们总会忍不住在所得税上作假。
@@
我们总会忍不住对配偶不忠。
@@
马可·奥勒留也面临过这种诱惑

cues.en: magnified a thousand fold,
cues.zh: 放大了一千倍，

cues.en: and he consistently
cues.zh: 他一直

cues.en: does good stuff.
cues.zh: 效果不错。

cues.en: Stop and think about this for a minute. This is no common man. This is not like the rest of us, and I don't know how he did it. Maybe he did it through philosophy, but,
cues.zh: 停下来想一想，只需一分钟。这可不是普通人。他跟我们其他人不一样，我不知道他是怎么做到的。也许他是通过哲学做到的，但是，

cues.en: well, it remains to be seen.
cues.zh: 嗯，这还有待观察。

cues.en: Marcus is the last of the good emperors. He's the last of the Antonine emperors,
cues.zh: Marcus是最后一位好皇帝。他是安东尼王朝的最后一位皇帝，

cues.en: and the emperors that come before him are, generally speaking, okay. They're not as bad as the ones that come after,
cues.zh: 而在他之前的那些皇帝，一般来说还算可以。他们不像之后的那些皇帝那么糟糕，

cues.en: but
cues.zh: 但是

cues.en: Marcus is perhaps the greatest of the Romans, the noblest of the Romans. When old fashioned writers talk about Roman virtue, what they have in mind is Marcus Aurelius,
cues.zh: Marcus也许是罗马人中最伟大的、最高尚的。当老派作家谈论罗马美德时，他们想到的就是Marcus Aurelius，

cues.en: a man who does what he ought to do regardless of circumstance.
cues.zh: 一个不论处境如何都会做自己该做之事的人。

cues.en: Tough Roman virtue. He's not afraid of being dead. He's not afraid of
cues.zh: 坚韧的罗马美德。他不怕死亡。他不怕

cues.en: being in pain. He's not afraid of having people laugh at him. He's only afraid of doing what's wrong.
cues.zh: 身处痛苦。他不怕被人嘲笑。他唯一怕的是做错事。

cues.en: He's only afraid of making chaos of his soul. Why? Because his soul is the only thing he's completely
cues.zh: 他唯一怕的是让自己的灵魂陷入混乱。为什么？因为他的灵魂是他唯一完全

cues.en: in control of. It's the only thing he's responsible for, and the rest of it is a matter of indifference to him. He'll certainly try and perform his function as emperor in the best way he possibly can,
cues.zh: 掌控的东西。那是他唯一需要负责的东西，其余的一切对他来说都无所谓。他当然会尽力以最好的方式履行自己作为皇帝的职责，

cues.en: but there are Germans at the border, and should they succeed in winning this war, he did the best he could. He has no reason to feel guilty. He has no reason to feel that this is a difficulty.
cues.zh: 但边境上有日耳曼人，如果他们真赢下了这场战争，那他也已经尽了全力。他没有理由感到内疚。他没有理由觉得这是什么难事。

cues.en: If, for some reason, he gets sick, well, sickness is part of human life. You accept it as it is, you deal with it the best you can, and then you move on. In other words, Marcus Aurelius intends to live a life which he will not have to feel guilty about anything,
cues.zh: 如果因为某种原因他病了，那疾病本来就是人生的一部分。你接受它本来的样子，尽力应对，然后继续前行。换句话说，Marcus Aurelius想要过一种不必为任何事感到内疚的生活，

cues.en: and he succeeded in doing that under the most trying
cues.zh: 而他在最艰难的

cues.en: possible circumstances.
cues.zh: 处境下做到了这一点。

cues.en: Again, put yourself in a position where you can have anything you want, and no one can stop you. No matter how evil, no matter how depraved, no one can stop you because your word is law. Marcus Aurelius behaved himself for nineteen years under those circumstances.
cues.zh: 再想想，假设你处于这样一个位置：你可以拥有任何想要的东西，而且没人能阻止你。无论多么邪恶，无论多么堕落，都没人能阻拦你，因为你的一言一行就是律法。奥勒留（Marcus Aurelius）在那种环境下坚守了十九年。

cues.en: It's a standing reproach to our self indulgence.
cues.zh: 这简直是对我们放纵自己的常态诘问。

cues.en: The kind of things that Marcus Aurelius writes are not meant for publication. Let's think about this a little further.
cues.zh: 奥勒留写的这些东西本就不是为了出版。让我们再深入思考一下。

cues.en: Marcus wrote this manuscript without intending to have it published. After his death, he wanted to have it burned.
cues.zh: 奥勒留写这份手稿时根本没打算出版。他死后，还曾想把它烧掉。

cues.en: Some
cues.zh: 某个

cues.en: philosophically inclined,
cues.zh: 有哲学倾向的——

cues.en: I guess, bookkeeper, librarian,
cues.zh: 我猜，大概是记账员、图书管理员、

cues.en: aide de camp, or whoever it is that picked this up, said, no, we just can't throw this out. We cannot lose the memory of such a great man, and we can't lose the sort of meditations that he created. He wrote a book called The Meditations,
cues.zh: 副官，或是其他什么捡起它的人，说，不，我们绝不能把它扔掉。我们不能失去这样一位伟人的记忆，也不能失去他所创造的这种沉思录。他写了一本书，叫做《沉思录》，

cues.en: and it's a book to himself that's not intended to be published.
cues.zh: 这是一本写给自己、根本没打算出版的书。

cues.en: What sort of a man writes a book to himself?
cues.zh: 什么样的人会写一本写给自己的书？

cues.en: What sense does that make? Think about it. The nature of a book is communicating something, and we would think we would communicate it to some reader, But this is not going be published. It's written to himself. What makes a man write a book to himself?
cues.zh: 这有什么意义呢？想想看。书的本质是传达某些内容，我们通常认为它是传达给某个读者的，但这本不会出版。它是写给自己的。是什么驱使一个人写一本写给自己的书？

cues.en: And there's a very deep answer, I think, here.
cues.zh: 我想，这里有一个非常深刻的答案。

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius writes a book to himself because he's the loneliest man in the world.
cues.zh: 奥勒留写一本写给自己的书，是因为他是世界上最孤独的人。

cues.en: He has no friends because he has no equals.
cues.zh: 他没有朋友，因为没有人能与他平起平坐。

cues.en: Think about a man breaking himself on the rock of an impossible virtue.
cues.zh: 想象一下，一个人为了追求一种遥不可及的道德，将自己撞得粉身碎骨。

cues.en: He has no equals. Everyone he talks to wants something from him. He is the emperor of everything in the world. He owns it all. Everything he says immediately gets done. He has absolute life and death power over everyone.
cues.zh: 无人能与他比肩。每一个和他交谈的人，都想从他身上索取些什么。他是世间万物的帝王，坐拥一切。言出必行。他掌握着所有人的生杀大权。

cues.en: So anytime he's in the throne room, he's having an audience, someone comes in from some part of the empire, they're always here for some reason, and they're always here because they want something from him. And all Marcus wants to do is live a philosophical life, but he happens to have had the misfortune to be born the emperor of Rome.
cues.zh: 所以无论何时他身处大殿接见臣民，帝国各处来的人总有各种由头，而且无一不是想从他身上索取。而 Marcus 唯一想做的是过哲学家的生活，可他偏偏不幸生为罗马皇帝。

cues.en: What a pity.
cues.zh: 何其悲哀。

cues.en: So he has to deal with these self centered, swinish people all the time, and it's his responsibility to do good for them, to give them justice,
cues.zh: 所以他必须时刻应付这些自私自利、贪婪卑劣的人，而他的职责却是要善待他们，给予他们公正，

cues.en: to give them both
cues.zh: 既为他们树立

cues.en: examples of virtue and virtuous laws and virtuous decisions,
cues.zh: 道德的典范，也带去公正的法律与决策，

cues.en: and the weariness of it gets to him after a while. The book that he's written, The Meditations, is shot through with a kind of philosophical melancholy
cues.zh: 久而久之，这种疲惫感击垮了他。他写下的那本书 The Meditations，通篇弥漫着一种哲学上的忧郁，

cues.en: that is extremely moving despite the stoic content of what he's saying. In other words, oddly enough, there are very few books in the world which generate more pathos,
cues.zh: 尽管他讲的是斯多葛派的内容，却极为打动人心。换句话说，奇妙的是，世上极少有哪本书能激发出如此强烈的悲怆，

cues.en: which create more of a sense of pity for a person reading this,
cues.zh: 能让读者心中升起如此深切的怜悯，

cues.en: than this book. He's writing a book to himself because he has no one else to talk to. And what kind of things does he write in the book? Moral maxims. I mean, has two or three ideas. It's something about a 100 odd pages, but he says essentially the same thing again and again and again. Why? He has nobody to talk to, so that limits the scope of his conversations.
cues.zh: 都比不上这本书。他写书是给自己看的，因为他找不到可以交谈的人。那他在书里写了什么？道德箴言。其实翻来覆去就两三个观点。全书大概有一百来页，但他基本上是一遍又一遍地说着同样的话。为什么？因为他无人可倾诉，这也限制了他思想交流的广度。

cues.en: And he's constantly trying to remind himself that, look, although the people you're dealing with are corrupt, evil, and depraved, it's your job not to get angry with them, but to try and teach them and morally improve them. If you can't morally improve them, at least put up with them, because the gods have created us, social animals,
cues.zh: 他不断提醒自己，看吧，尽管你打交道的人腐败、邪恶又堕落，你的职责不是对他们发怒，而是努力教导他们，在道德上改善他们。如果你无法在道德上改善他们，至少容忍他们，因为神把我们创造成社会性动物，

cues.en: and it is part of the mark, or it is the mark of a philosophical man that he should return benefits for harm, because those that would harm other people do not live the philosophical life.
cues.zh: 而以德报怨是哲学之人的标志，因为那些想伤害他人的人并没有过哲学的生活。

cues.en: Those that don't want
cues.zh: 那些不想

cues.en: the ultimate good for themselves and for society
cues.zh: 为自己和社会追求终极善的人

cues.en: do so because they don't know any better. Marcus has not only political power,
cues.zh: 之所以如此，是因为他们不明事理。马库斯不仅有政治权力，

cues.en: but wisdom,
cues.zh: 还有智慧，

cues.en: and in that respect, he's the only example in the Western tradition of any ruler who even remotely approximates
cues.zh: 在这方面，他是西方传统中唯一一位哪怕勉强接近

cues.en: Plato's philosopher king.
cues.zh: 柏拉图哲学王的统治者。

cues.en: And he has some of the qualities that Plato thought the philosopher king would have. He is totally disdainful of wealth. Why? He owns everything. What would it be like to own everything from England to Egypt?
cues.zh: 他具备柏拉图认为哲学王应有的一些品质。他完全鄙视财富。为什么？因为他拥有一切。从英格兰到埃及，拥有一切是什么感觉？

cues.en: Well, the idea of accumulating more stuff becomes less and less interesting if you stop and think about it.
cues.zh: 嗯，如果你停下来想一想，积累更多东西的念头会变得越来越无趣。

cues.en: And if you can have sex with, say, a million people, the million at first has very limited attraction.
cues.zh: 如果你能和比如一百万人发生性关系，那一百万起初的吸引力非常有限。

cues.en: And at that point he stops to think and he says, I will do my best to constantly do what I ought to do.
cues.zh: 那时他停下来思考，他说，我会尽力不断做我该做的事。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而且

cues.en: there is a sort of
cues.zh: 这本书带有一种

cues.en: whistling in the graveyard tone to this book. He is, in some respects, an enormously lonely man, and in some respects, an enormously sad man. There's a melancholite in this that's terrifically moving.
cues.zh: “吹着口哨走过坟地”般的悲凉基调。他在某些方面是个极其孤独的人，在另一些方面又是个极其悲伤的人。其中流露出一种极其感人的忧郁。

cues.en: And yet,
cues.zh: 然而，

cues.en: we ought not to pity Marcus Aurelius, because if he looked at our lives, he would pity us.
cues.zh: 我们实在不该同情马可·奥勒留，因为如果他审视我们的生活，他反倒会同情我们。

cues.en: Pathetic creatures that we are, we don't even meet his standard of virtue, and we're pitying him.
cues.zh: 我们这些可怜的生物连他的美德标准都达不到，居然还在同情他。

cues.en: Think about the irony of that. He said, Well, I'd pity you back if I didn't think that was disrespectful.
cues.zh: 想想这其中的讽刺意味吧。他会说，好吧，要不是觉得那样不够尊重人，我也会反过来同情你的。

cues.en: Think about what it takes to be something like Marcus Aurelius. We shall not see his
cues.zh: 想想看，要成为像马可·奥勒留那样的人需要付出什么。我们再也见不到

cues.en: like again.
cues.zh: 这样的人物了。

cues.en: In the book itself,
cues.zh: 在这本书里，

cues.en: he has all kinds of intriguing
cues.zh: 他有着各种引人入胜的

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 甚至可以说

cues.en: caustic, if you will, moral maxims. He says things like this,
cues.zh: 带有讽刺意味的道德格言。他会说这样的话：

cues.en: Soon you will have forgotten all things,
cues.zh: 很快你就会忘掉一切，

cues.en: and soon all things will have forgotten you.
cues.zh: 很快一切也会忘掉你。

cues.en: In other words, don't get overwrought. You're angry with this guy just because he didn't do what he was supposed to do? Ask yourself how many of the people that are working for you are doing what they're supposed to do.
cues.zh: 换句话说，别太激动。你生这家伙的气，不就是因为他没按规矩办事吗？问问你自己，手底下有多少人在按规矩办事？

cues.en: Soon, you'll have forgotten all this, because you'll be dead. And soon, old people who know you, they're going be dead too, and they'll have forgotten you. And so what's the point of being mean to people?
cues.zh: 很快，你就会把这一切忘光，因为你就要死了。不久之后，认识你的老人们也都会死去，他们也会把你忘得精光。所以，对别人尖酸刻薄有什么意义呢？

cues.en: Now, imagine the kind of philosophical self restraint we're talking about here. This is a guy who can chop everyone's head off if he gets sufficiently angry, so he never does.
cues.zh: 现在，想象一下我们所说的这种哲学上的自我克制。这家伙要是发起火来本可以把所有人的头都砍掉，但他从没这么做过。

cues.en: Remarkable, remarkable.
cues.zh: 太精彩了，太精彩了。

cues.en: So Marcus Aurelius is a man who constantly, in his book, is writing short one and two line epigrams
cues.zh: 所以马可·奥勒留这个人，在他的书里不断地写下一两行的警句，

cues.en: that essentially say things like, Don't lose your temper with these people, Marcus, you know how they are.
cues.zh: 基本上都是在说：别跟这些人发脾气啊，马可，你知道他们是什么样的人。

cues.en: Marcus, it's not your fault that they're stupid. You tried to teach them, and you can keep on trying to teach them, but if Socrates was a good man and they killed him, what do you expect them to do to you?
cues.zh: 马可，他们笨又不是你的错。你试着教过他们了，你也可以继续试着教他们，但如果苏格拉底是个好人他们还把他杀了，你指望他们会对你怎样？

cues.en: On the other hand,
cues.zh: 另一方面，

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius is willing to rule the Roman Empire for the same reason that the Platonic philosopher king is. If he gives up, somebody worse is gonna take the job, and you know what happens then. Right? He'd much rather just go home and read his books. He doesn't wanna listen to this stuff.
cues.zh: 马可·奥勒留愿意统治罗马帝国，原因和柏拉图式的哲学王一样。如果他放弃了，就会有更糟糕的人来接替这个职位，你知道那样会发生什么。对吧？他其实更愿意回家去读他的书。他根本不想听这些破事。

cues.en: But he says, well, the gods put me here. I didn't ask for this job, but I can't very well give it up. I'd be abdicating my responsibility to other people. Imagine the bad laws and bad emperors were gonna get after me.
cues.zh: 但他说，好吧，是神把我放在这里的。我可没求着要这份工作，但我又不能轻易放弃。那样我就等于对其他人推卸了责任。想象一下我走之后会来什么样的恶法和昏君吧。

cues.en: Well, should I give the job up now, or stand here until the gods are good enough to relieve me of my post?
cues.zh: 那么，我是现在就把工作辞了呢，还是在这里站好岗，直到神发善心把我撤职？

cues.en: In fact, that's the metaphor he uses all the time. The gods have put you on guard over the Roman Empire. Everyone else is sleeping. Stay where you are and stay awake, elsewise God knows what's going to happen.
cues.zh: 事实上，这就是他经常使用的比喻。神把你派去守卫罗马帝国。其他所有人都在睡觉。坚守岗位，保持清醒，否则鬼才知道会发生什么。

cues.en: Marcus Aureus is constantly whistling his way through the graveyard, trying to tell him that this is a very happy life, that he loves being a philosopher, and he particularly loves the particular portion of reality that gods have assigned to him.
cues.zh: 马可·奥勒留不断地在墓地里吹着口哨给自己壮胆，试图告诉自己这是一种非常幸福的生活，他热爱当哲学家，尤其热爱神分配给他的那份特定的现实。

cues.en: Now, I think that everyone believes this except the people that read this book, which perhaps is why it wasn't supposed to be published, because when you look at this, you see a terrifically lonely man, a man of immense moral heroism,
cues.zh: 现在，我认为除了读过这本书的人之外，大家都相信这一点，也许这就是它本不该出版的原因，因为当你看到这些时，你看到的是一个极其孤独的人，一个有着巨大道德英雄气概的人，

cues.en: who has no shoulder to cry on, who disdains crying because what's the point of crying?
cues.zh: 他没有可以哭诉的肩膀，他鄙视哭泣，因为哭泣有什么意义呢？

cues.en: We must live in accordance with nature. Now here's the natural condition of human beings: they get born, all kinds of stuff happens to them, and they die.
cues.zh: 我们必须依照自然本性生活。而这就是人类的自然状况：他们出生，各种事情发生在他们身上，然后他们死去。

cues.en: Marcus' maxims with reference to that are A, stop complaining. There's nothing to complain about because there's only two kinds of things. There are the kinds of things you can control, and there are the kinds of things you can't. If you can't control it, complaining about it is stupid and a waste of time, I don't want to hear any more about it, because you can't control it, so what's point of talking about this? Or you have the other kind of thing, the kind of thing you can control, like your intentions,
cues.zh: 马库斯对此的格言是：第一，停止抱怨。没有什么可抱怨的，因为只有两类事情。一类是你能控制的事情，另一类是你无法控制的事情。如果你无法控制它，抱怨它就是愚蠢且浪费时间，我不想再听到任何关于它的话，因为你无法控制它，那谈论它有什么意义呢？或者你有另一类事情，你能控制的事情，比如你的意图，

cues.en: like your behavior, like your actions. And since you can control them, who do you expect to help you out except yourself? Stop complaining about that too. So whether it's the kind of thing you can control, or it's the kind of thing you can control, Marcus Aurelius does not want to hear any complaints, and he does not want to hear any excuses, because there are no excuses to give.
cues.zh: 比如你的行为，比如你的行动。既然你能控制它们，除了你自己，你还指望谁来帮你呢？所以也不要再抱怨那个了。因此，无论那是你能控制的事情，还是你能控制的事情，马库斯·奥勒留都不想听到任何抱怨，他也不想听到任何借口，因为没有任何借口可给。

cues.en: Now,
cues.zh: 现在，

cues.en: that's easy enough to say, and a lot of people think that other people should be this way.
cues.zh: 说起来容易，很多人都觉得别人应该做到这样。

cues.en: Right? Have you noticed it? You can't help but admire this guy. Every one of us, I've been in this audience, thought, wow, what a great guy. I wish I knew him personally. No, you don't. Think of what he'd think of you.
cues.zh: 对吧？你注意到了吗？你忍不住会钦佩这家伙。我们每个人，包括坐在观众席上的我，都会想，哇，多好的人啊。真希望我认识他。不，你并不想。想想他会怎么看你。

cues.en: You really don't want to know this guy. Imagine working for him? Oh,
cues.zh: 你真的不想认识这家伙。想象一下为他工作？哦，

cues.en: please. No, this guy is never going to be satisfied. And if he is satisfied, he's not like he's gonna give you applause. He's gonna say, well, you're doing what you ought to do. No compliments for you. You're doing what you ought to do. You don't need any reward beyond that. You're living like a philosophical man, which is a reward in itself. Virtue is its own reward. You're virtuous. What do you want from me? Back to work.
cues.zh: 拜托。不，这家伙永远不会满意。就算他满意了，他也不会给你鼓掌。他会说，嗯，你做了你该做的事。不会夸你。你做了该做的事。除此之外你不需要任何奖励。你像个哲学家一样活着，这本身就是奖励。美德本身就是回报。你有美德。你还想从我这儿要什么？回去干活。

cues.en: And of course, if you're not virtuous, you are pretty much what he expects human beings to be, you swine.
cues.zh: 当然，如果你没有美德，你基本上就是他预料中的人类样子，你这头猪。

cues.en: And what's unnerving about this is that there's not the slightest taint of hypocrisy in it. He not only says
cues.zh: 令人不安的是，这里面没有一丝一毫的虚伪。他不仅说

cues.en: this stuff, he acts this stuff.
cues.zh: 这些话，他还付诸行动。

cues.en: He not only talks the talk, he walks the walk. He does it. And he does it under worse, more difficult circumstances than you. Fail to do it.
cues.zh: 他不仅嘴上说，还真这么做。他做到了。而且他是在比你更糟、更难的处境下做到的。你却没做到。

cues.en: And yet he still likes us. In other words, he'd still go out of his way to help us out.
cues.zh: 然而他还是喜欢我们。换句话说，他仍然会特意来帮我们。

cues.en: If he were the judge in a court of law, he would still give us justice, even though we have done nothing to deserve it. As a matter of fact, we what is it that that that... What's the line from Hamlet? If we gave every man his desserts, who would escape a whipping? Marcus Aurelius would. That's part of the problem with Marcus Aurelius. There's nothing quite like this guy in the whole history of the world.
cues.zh: 如果他是法庭上的法官，他仍然会给我们公正，尽管我们根本不配。事实上，我们……那句……《哈姆雷特》里那句台词是什么来着？如果按每个人的功过论处，谁逃得了一顿鞭子？马可·奥勒留逃得了。这就是马可·奥勒留的部分问题所在。纵观整个世界历史，都找不到像他这样的人。

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius says things in his book
cues.zh: Marcus Aurelius 在他的书中写过这样的话

cues.en: like,
cues.zh: 比如，

cues.en: human beings are social animals. Either teach them or put up with them.
cues.zh: 人类是社会性动物。要么教导他们，要么容忍他们。

cues.en: The kind of thing that a man has to remind himself of, I imagine.
cues.zh: 我想，这是一个人不得不时刻提醒自己的道理。

cues.en: Or Marcus says in another passage,
cues.zh: 或者 Marcus 在另一段中写道，

cues.en: Are you weary of enduring the bad men of the world?
cues.zh: 你是否厌倦了忍受世上的恶人？

cues.en: The gods aren't, and they made them.
cues.zh: 神明可不觉得厌倦，而且正是他们创造了恶人。

cues.en: Are you really weary of enduring the bad men of the world, especially given that you're one of them?
cues.zh: 你真的厌倦了忍受世上的恶人吗，特别是考虑到你自己也是其中一员？

cues.en: Dreadful,
cues.zh: 可怕，

cues.en: powerful,
cues.zh: 有力，

cues.en: caustic,
cues.zh: 尖刻，

cues.en: ruthless
cues.zh: 毫不留情地

cues.en: analysis of himself and others.
cues.zh: 剖析了自己与他人。

cues.en: He pulls no punches.
cues.zh: 他从不手软。

cues.en: He is an honest man, and how many honest politicians are there in the world? I mean, it's been some time since we had one leave us literary remains, and here we certainly do have one.
cues.zh: 他是一个诚实的人，这世上有多少诚实的政治家？我的意思是，自从我们有一位留下文学遗产的政治家以来已经过去很久了，而这里我们确实就有一位。

cues.en: The Stoics put together an important and I think worthwhile idea, particularly in this day of international politics,
cues.zh: 斯多葛学派提出了一个重要且我认为很有价值的观点，尤其是在当今的国际政治背景下，

cues.en: and that's the idea of a cosmopolitan
cues.zh: 那就是关于大同世界（cosmopolitan）的

cues.en: political philosophy.
cues.zh: 政治哲学。

cues.en: There's few people as cosmopolitan,
cues.zh: 很少有人能像 Marcus Aurelius 那样

cues.en: as
cues.zh: 具有大同胸怀、

cues.en: lacking in provincial qualities as Marcus Aurelius.
cues.zh: 毫无狭隘地方观念。

cues.en: The stoic wise man has made his life consistent with nature, and nature is universal in everywhere. It exists in every place and every time. So the Stoic man is never any place but home.
cues.zh: 斯多葛派的智者让自己的生活顺应自然，而自然是无处不在、普适的。它存在于每一个地方和每一个时代。因此，斯多葛派的人无论身处何地，都如同在家。

cues.en: His
cues.zh: 他的

cues.en: polis
cues.zh: 城邦

cues.en: is the cosmos.
cues.zh: 就是整个宇宙。

cues.en: That is what makes him cosmopolitan.
cues.zh: 正是这一点让他成为了世界公民。

cues.en: In ancient Greek political theory, you were a citizen of one political polis, of one particular polis, one particular city state. You were an Athenian or you were you were a Spartan. The stoic wise man is cosmopolitan.
cues.zh: 在古希腊政治理论中，你是某个政治城邦的公民，属于某个特定的城邦、某个特定的城邦国家。你是雅典人，或者是斯巴达人。而斯多葛派的智者则是世界公民。

cues.en: Wherever he is, he lives in accordance with nature.
cues.zh: 无论他在哪里，他都顺应自然而生活。

cues.en: Whatever he does, he does what he knows to be right. What difference does it make whether he's in a jail cell or in a palace?
cues.zh: 无论他做什么，他都做自己认为正确的事。他在监狱里还是在宫殿里，又有什么区别呢？

cues.en: As Marcus Aurelius put it in a beautiful epigram in the even in a palace it is possible to live well.
cues.zh: 正如马可·奥勒留在一句优美的警句中所说，即使在宫殿里，也完全可以过得很好。

cues.en: No
cues.zh: 没有

cues.en: excuses. Don't tell me that it's because of temptation, that won't go over. No excuses go with Marcus.
cues.zh: 借口。别跟我说什么是因为受到了诱惑，那行不通。在马可这里没有任何借口可讲。

cues.en: The idea of a cosmopolitan political philosophy
cues.zh: 世界主义政治哲学的理念

cues.en: is one of the great achievements of Roman Stoicism, and if you stop and think about it, it's an excellent and a necessary idea when you're running something as big and heterogeneous as the Roman Empire.
cues.zh: 是罗马斯多葛主义的伟大成就之一。你停下来想想就会发现，当你统治着像罗马帝国这样庞大且多元的庞然大物时，这是一个极好且不可或缺的理念。

cues.en: This tremendously complicated mix of religions and cultures and peoples and all kinds of heterogeneous ideas
cues.zh: 这种极其复杂的宗教、文化、民族以及各种异质思想的交织

cues.en: means that
cues.zh: 意味着

cues.en: this is going to be a big patchwork, a big quilt. It's not going to be one culturally unified area. But Marcus would be just as happy being a slave as he is being an emperor. He would just as happy being a Gaul or an Egyptian as a Roman. As long as there is a nature there, and there is a human spirit which can be made in accordance with nature, any of the external facts of life don't matter.
cues.zh: 这里将是一个巨大的大杂烩，一块巨大的拼布。它不会是一个文化上单一统一的地区。但马可无论作为奴隶还是作为皇帝，都会同样快乐。无论是作为高卢人、埃及人还是罗马人，他都会同样快乐。只要自然存在，只要存在能够顺应自然的人类精神，任何外部的生活现实都无关紧要。

cues.en: And now, for the first time, we can perhaps see why the Roman Stoics have a reputation, to some extent deserved, of being kind of harsh, cold, unfeeling men, because there's nothing to worry about, and it's hard for them to sympathize with the fact that other people are worried about things that they regard as trivial or not worth worrying about at all. Many of us worry about sickness.
cues.zh: 现在，我们或许终于明白为什么罗马斯多葛主义者会给人一种在某种程度上确实如此的冷酷、无情之感了，因为根本没有什么好担心的，他们很难去同情其他人，因为别人在担心那些他们认为微不足道或根本不值得担忧的事情。我们许多人都为疾病而担忧。

cues.en: Well, Marcus Aurelius will point out that all people get sick.
cues.zh: 嗯，Marcus Aurelius 会指出，所有人都会生病。

cues.en: And once you get sick, since you're a rational
cues.zh: 一旦你生病了，既然你是个理性的人

cues.en: human being, you want to go to the doctor, do what he prescribes, and fix your body. There's no point in complaining any place along the line because you know what you're supposed to do. Go do it. Stop asking for somebody else to help you. If you don't help yourself, how can you expect anybody else to help you?
cues.zh:
作为人类，你想去看医生，遵照医嘱，然后把身体治好。
@@
在整个过程中抱怨没有任何意义，因为你知道自己该做什么。
@@
去做吧。
@@
别再指望别人来帮你了。
@@
如果你连自己都不帮，又怎么能指望别人来帮你在呢？

cues.en: Which is a fair criticism.
cues.zh: 这是个合理的批评。

cues.en: It would be much less persuasive
cues.zh: 这样说就没有那么有说服力了

cues.en: and much less impressive if this were a sort of hypocritical philosophy,
cues.zh: 如果这是一种虚伪的哲学，那就不那么令人印象深刻了，

cues.en: where Marcus Aurelius indulged himself and told everyone else to be stoical.
cues.zh: 马库斯·奥勒留放纵自己，却要求其他人都要像斯多葛学派一样克制。

cues.en: What really makes this spring to life, what makes this persuasive and moving and important, is that he lives the life.
cues.zh: 真正让这一切变得生动、具有说服力、打动人心且至关重要的，是他身体力行地去践行了这种生活。

cues.en: So he doesn't complain when he gets sick. He doesn't complain when he meets military reverses. He doesn't complain about anything.
cues.zh: 所以他生病时从不抱怨，战事受挫时从不抱怨，他对任何事都毫无怨言。

cues.en: Who would we complain to? The
cues.zh: 我们该向谁投诉呢？那个

cues.en: buck does stop with Marcus Aureus. If you think of the chain of command in the Roman Empire, he he doesn't get to complain to anyone else. Everyone complains to him, and he's constantly listened to complaints and difficulties and problems, and he's watching people become unglued, and they're watching them get all upset, and watching them be greedy and avaricious and swinish and lustful, and all the things he's not.
cues.zh:
最终的责任还是落在了 Marcus Aureus 身上。如果你想想罗马帝国的指挥链，他根本没法向其他人抱怨。
@@
每个人都向他抱怨，他不得不 constamment 倾听各种抱怨、困难和问题，看着人们情绪崩溃，
@@
看着他们变得烦躁不安，看着他们贪婪、吝啬、像猪一样卑劣、充满欲望，而这些正是他所没有的特质。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: he is rather harsh in his criticism, and I think that that's a fair observation about him. But he's not hypocritical,
cues.zh: 他批评起来相当严厉，我认为这是对他一个公道的观察。但他并不虚伪，

cues.en: and he's not unfair.
cues.zh: 也并不不公正。

cues.en: And that's one of the cosmopolitan
cues.zh: 而这正是这种政治哲学和道德哲学中

cues.en: universal elements in this political philosophy and in this moral philosophy,
cues.zh: 普世性的要素之一，

cues.en: because the moral and political philosophy for Marcus Aurelius are going to be connected. In the same way that in Plato's Republic, politics was ethics writ large, and what was good for the individual soul, the gold, silver, and bronze, that ordering of the soul between reason, spirit, and desire,
cues.zh: 因为对马可·奥勒留来说，道德哲学和政治哲学是相连的。正如在柏拉图的《理想国》中，政治就是放大的伦理，对个体灵魂有益的东西，金、银、铜，灵魂在理性、精神与欲望之间的那种秩序，

cues.en: what's good for the soul is the same thing it's good for the city, to have rational people running the government like Marcus Aurelius, doing their best to follow the philosophical life. You'll want bravery and fortitude and courage among your soldiers, the silver virtues, and among the rest of the people, you expect the bronze virtues. They want to eat and drink and make merry. It would be nice if we could make philosophers all... Of all of them, but if we can't, the best thing we can do is to take care of them and prevent
cues.zh: 对灵魂有益的东西，对城邦也是同一回事，就是让理性的人像马可·奥勒留那样治理政府，尽力遵循哲学生活。你会希望士兵身上有勇敢和坚毅，即银的美德，而在其余民众身上，你期待的是铜的美德。他们想吃喝享乐。要是我们能让所有人都成为哲学家就好了……所有人，但若做不到，我们能做的最好之事就是照顾他们，防止

cues.en: misfortunes from befalling them, in some respects to try and save them from themselves.
cues.zh: 不幸降临到他们身上，在某些方面努力把他们从自身中拯救出来。

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius
cues.zh: 马可·奥勒留

cues.en: is
cues.zh: 是

cues.en: the only example of this in Roman culture.
cues.zh: 罗马文化中这方面的唯一例子。

cues.en: There's not a great deal of things that we can compare him to.
cues.zh: 我们没有太多东西可以拿来与他比较。

cues.en: If we had to say
cues.zh: 如果非要说

cues.en: that there was someone to compare him to, it would be Epictetus, the slave.
cues.zh: 有什么人可以与他相比，那就是奴隶爱比克泰德。

cues.en: And Epictetus and Marcus Aurelius could meet at a level of equality, even though the social distinctions between them are enormous and grave. The reason why they would meet at a level of equality: because they could share mutual respect,
cues.zh: 爱比克泰德和马可·奥勒留能够在平等的层面上相遇，尽管他们之间的社会阶层差异巨大而深重。他们之所以能在平等的层面上相遇：是因为他们能够共享相互的尊重，

cues.en: because they both understand that to have an orderly soul is the key thing in human life, and that's what makes life worth living.
cues.zh: 因为他们都明白，拥有一个有序的灵魂是人生中最关键的事，而这正是让生命值得活下去的东西。

cues.en: And whether you happen to be
cues.zh: 而无论你碰巧是

cues.en: a slave or an emperor doesn't make any difference. Whether you happen to be sick or healthy doesn't make any difference. Whether you happen to be just born and have a hundred years ahead of you, or whether you're on your deathbed doesn't make any difference.
cues.zh: 奴隶还是皇帝，都没有区别。无论你碰巧生病还是健康，都没有区别。无论你碰巧刚刚出生、前面还有一百年，还是你正躺在临终的床上，都没有区别。

cues.en: Marcus says,
cues.zh: 马可说，

cues.en: with regard to death, because many people are afraid of death, and he has no understanding. He doesn't really understand what everybody else's problem is. He says, look, everyone dies,
cues.zh: 关于死亡，因为许多人害怕死亡，而他并不理解。他并不真正理解别人的问题是什么。他说，看吧，每个人都会死，

cues.en: so you're gonna die.
cues.zh: 所以你也会死。

cues.en: So what's the point of complaining about it? I can understand trying to avoid it. I mean, health is a good thing, but when you're gonna die, you're gonna die. Don't give in to fear.
cues.zh: 那抱怨它有什么意义呢？我能理解试图避免它。我是说，健康是好事，但当你要死的时候，你就是要死了。不要屈服于恐惧。

cues.en: Don't give in to irrational
cues.zh: 不要屈服于非理性的

cues.en: musings.
cues.zh: 胡思乱想。

cues.en: Don't let your imagination run wild. Control your feelings.
cues.zh: 不要让你的想象肆意狂奔。控制你的感受。

cues.en: Control your emotions.
cues.zh: 控制你的情绪。

cues.en: Control that part of you which is you.
cues.zh: 控制你之中那个真正是你的部分。

cues.en: The meat, your body, not so important. The other stuff around you in the world, a matter of indifference to you. As long as you follow the way of nature, as long as you act in a rational fashion, as long as you live up to the best potentials in the human soul, then you are a good man and you need worry about nothing else.
cues.zh: 肉，你的身体，没那么重要。你周围世界中的其他东西，对你来说无关紧要。只要你遵循自然之道，只要你以理性的方式行事，只要你活出人类灵魂中最好的潜能，那么你就是一个好人，你无需担心其他任何事。

cues.en: Some people worry about the gods, that the gods will cause you misfortunes,
cues.zh: 有些人担心神灵，担心神灵会给你带来厄运，

cues.en: that the gods have a Hades or a Hell or an afterlife where people will be tortured and have bad things done to them. Marcus adopts exactly the same position that Socrates did. He says, look,
cues.zh: 担心神灵有冥界、地狱或某种来世，在那里人们会受折磨、遭受厄运。马可采取了与苏格拉底完全相同的立场。他说，听着，

cues.en: Marcus
cues.zh: 马可

cues.en: says, I'm not certain if there are gods. In
cues.zh: 说，我不能确定是否有神。在

cues.en: the book itself, he says, I'm not aware of any rational proof that there exist gods, and I'm not aware of any rational proof that there are no gods. In other words, he's agnostic in that respect. But he takes a position rather like that of Blaise Pascal,
cues.zh: 书里，他说，我不知道有什么理性的证据证明神存在，我也不知道有什么理性的证据证明神不存在。换句话说，他在这个方面是个不可知论者。但他采取了一种类似于布莱士·帕斯卡的立场，

cues.en: and he says, let's think about what the implications are if god exists, and let's think about what the implications are if he doesn't exist, and let's see if we can find one way of acting that'll satisfy both contingencies.
cues.zh: 并且他说，让我们想想如果神存在会有什么影响，让我们想想如果神不存在会有什么影响，然后看看我们能否找到一种能够兼顾这两种情况的行事方式。

cues.en: Logical guy.
cues.zh: 挺有逻辑的人。

cues.en: And he says, well, if the gods don't exist, and the world is just atoms and the void, if you think back to Professor Stalloff's lecture about early primitive
cues.zh: 他说，好吧，如果神不存在，世界仅仅是原子与虚空——如果你回想起斯塔洛夫教授关于早期原始

cues.en: physical theories, well, we have atoms and the void, homogeneous
cues.zh: 物理学理论的讲座，我们有原子和虚空，

cues.en: stuff called matter, and then the space that it moves around in. Well, if there are no gods, and there is no moral order to the world, and we're just atoms in the void, well, what difference does it make what happens to you or anybody else? So you come into being, you go out of being, so what? You get healthy, you get sick, so what? There's nothing to get excited about because, well, it's just atoms in the void. Don't be afraid of it. It is what it is. There's nothing to be afraid of. You could say that Roman stoicism is a way of telling people, there's nothing to be afraid of. Nothing can happen to you in nature that is not a part of nature, and nature contains nothing fearful for the rational soul.
cues.zh: 被称为物质的同质材料，以及它在其中运动的空间。好吧，如果没有神，世界也没有道德秩序，而我们只是原子和虚空，那么发生在你或任何人身上的事又有什么区别呢？所以你诞生了，你消亡了，那又怎样？你健康了，你生病了，那又怎样？没什么好大惊小怪的，因为，好吧，这只是原子和虚空。不要害怕。它就是这样。没什么好害怕的。你可以说罗马斯多葛学派是一种告诉人们的方法：没什么好害怕的。自然中不会发生任何不属于自然一部分的事情，而对于理性的灵魂来说，自然并不包含任何可怕的东西。

cues.en: Now let's take the other half of
cues.zh: 现在我们来看

cues.en: the Pascalian
cues.zh: 帕斯卡式抉择的

cues.en: alternative.
cues.zh: 另一面。

cues.en: Let's consider the proposition that there are gods or a god. It doesn't matter whether it's monotheistic or polytheistic.
cues.zh: 我们来假设真有神存在，不管是一神论还是多神论都无所谓。

cues.en: If there are gods,
cues.zh: 如果真有神，

cues.en: then they must be rather like the gods of
cues.zh: 那他们必定很像

cues.en: They are all good. They are all wise. They are all completely moral and completely virtuous and completely knowing and completely excellent.
cues.zh: 至善至智的存在，拥有完全的道德、美德，全知且全能。

cues.en: Would creatures like this do anything bad to you? Well,
cues.zh: 这样的存在会伤害你吗？呃，

cues.en: maybe they would. Maybe if you've been doing bad stuff, maybe there is something actually in store for you later on. There may well be a Hades. Gods like that may want to create moral order in the world and dish out to the bad people of the world just what they have coming to them.
cues.zh: 也许会。如果你一直在做坏事，也许之后真的会有报应等着你。很可能会有地狱存在。这样的神明可能会想在世间建立道德秩序，让恶人得到应有的下场。

cues.en: But suppose, hypothetically, you lived according to reason and according to nature and according to the universal law of the Logos.
cues.zh: 但假设你顺应理性、顺应自然，遵循逻各斯（Logos）的普世法则去生活。

cues.en: Would the gods hurt a man like that, or would a man like that be a friend of the gods?
cues.zh: 神会伤害这样的人吗？还是说这样的人会成为神的朋友？

cues.en: And if a man like that would be dealt with fairly by the gods, justly by the gods, and well by the gods, the gods will do you no harm.
cues.zh: 如果神会公平、公正、良善地对待这样的人，那神就不会伤害你。

cues.en: So there are two possibilities.
cues.zh: 所以有两种可能。

cues.en: Either the world is atoms in the void, the world is just stuff, in which case there's nothing to be afraid of because you're just part of that stuff, you might as well go along with the flow. Relax. Enjoy the ride.
cues.zh: 要么世界只是虚空中的原子，世界不过是物质构成的，那完全没什么好怕的，因为你不过是这些物质的一部分，不如顺其自然。放轻松，享受这段旅程。

cues.en: Nothing to be scared of. Nothing to get excited about.
cues.zh: 没什么好怕的，也没什么好激动的。

cues.en: On the other hand, and this, I suspect, deep down in Marcus is what he really believes,
cues.zh: 另一方面，我猜想，马库斯内心深处真正相信的是，

cues.en: I mean, when you just read between the lines and find out what the man himself is like, he does basically believe in the gods. Even though he doesn't know, if he had to place a wager either way, same way as Pascal, but perhaps not for the same reasons, he would say, yes, I believe in the gods. And if the gods exist, then they create moral order, and they are perfectly moral themselves, and they are perfectly just and good and righteous themselves, and they will do you no harm. So if there is an afterlife and you behave well, the gods will do you no harm because you deserve no harm done to you.
cues.zh: 我是说，当你从字里行间去体会，了解这个人本身是什么样的时候，他其实是相信神明的。尽管他自己并不确定，但如果他必须下个赌注，就像帕斯卡那样，不过也许理由不同，他会说，是的，我相信神明。而如果神明存在，那他们就创造了道德秩序，他们自身也是完美道德的，他们自身完美公正、善良、正直，他们不会伤害你。所以如果有来世，而你行为端正，神明不会伤害你，因为你不该受到伤害。

cues.en: If there is an afterlife and you behave badly, you have no one to blame but yourself.
cues.zh: 如果有来世，而你行为不端，那你只能怪自己。

cues.en: In every case, the only thing that a man is
cues.zh: 无论在哪种情况下，一个人唯一能

cues.en: in control of is the individual ego, himself,
cues.zh: 掌控的就是个体自我，他自己，

cues.en: the cogito, what Descartes will later on call the cogito,
cues.zh: 那个“我思”，也就是笛卡尔后来所说的“我思”，

cues.en: the self. If you are in control of that, if you have an orderly soul, then you have a divine soul, a good soul, and your life is worth living. The gods will not penalize you for that.
cues.zh: 那个自我。如果你能掌控它，如果你的灵魂井然有序，那你就拥有一个神圣的灵魂、一个善良的灵魂，你的生命就值得过。神明不会因此惩罚你。

cues.en: So, what's there to worry about? Don't worry, be happy.
cues.zh: 所以，有什么好担心的？别担心，开心点。

cues.en: Either world is atoms in the void, nothing to worry about. If the gods are there, well then, the gods certainly aren't going to hurt you. Either way,
cues.zh: 要么世界是虚空中的原子，没什么好担心的。如果神明存在，那好吧，神明肯定不会伤害你。无论哪种情况，

cues.en: don't worry, be happy. Do what you know you ought to do. Meet your moral obligations.
cues.zh: 别担心，开心点。做你知道自己该做的事。履行你的道德义务。

cues.en: In some respect, and I think that this is worth taking notes on if you happen to be here at the Kant lecture next week, or two weeks from now, is that the Stoic conception of virtue
cues.zh: 在某些方面——如果你下周或两周后来听康德的讲座，这点很值得记一下——斯多葛学派的美德观

cues.en: is an anticipation
cues.zh: 可以说是

cues.en: of what I will call the Kantian conception of virtue. Those of you who are familiar with the works of Immanuel Kant
cues.zh: 我所谓的康德式美德观的先驱。熟悉 Immanuel Kant 著作的人

cues.en: can recognize
cues.zh: 都能看出，

cues.en: the single-minded
cues.zh: 那种坚定不移、

cues.en: and ruthless
cues.zh: 甚至毫不妥协地

cues.en: acquirement of virtue as being the Kantian conception of of moral action or good moral behavior, and the Stoic conception as well. Both Kant and Marcus Aurelius have
cues.zh: 追求美德，既是康德对道德行为或崇高道德举止的定义，也是斯多葛学派的观点。Kant 和 Marcus Aurelius 都

cues.en: achieved the greatness that comes from being aware that virtue
cues.zh: 达到了一种伟大，即深刻意识到美德

cues.en: is sufficient in itself.
cues.zh: 本身就已足够。

cues.en: The single-minded pursuit of rationality,
cues.zh: 对理性的执着追求，

cues.en: of justice,
cues.zh: 对正义的追求，

cues.en: of temperance,
cues.zh: 对节制的追求，

cues.en: of fortitude,
cues.zh: 对坚毅的追求，

cues.en: is what this book is all about.
cues.zh: 正是这本书的核心所在。

cues.en: And in some respects, I feel
cues.zh: 在某种程度上，我甚至觉得

cues.en: a little bit like a voyeur in
cues.zh: 自己有点像个偷窥者，

cues.en: opening up a manuscript that Marcus
cues.zh: 翻开了一部 Marcus

cues.en: never meant to publish. And doubtless, he would be nothing except embarrassed if he knew that people were reading this book, because he wouldn't want to show that crack
cues.zh: 从未打算发表的手稿。毫无疑问，如果他知道人们在读这本书，一定会感到无比尴尬，因为他绝不想暴露出

cues.en: in the stoic face, right? He doesn't want to give people the idea that he ever worries or ever gets upset at all. In other words, doubtless, if he's in heaven,
cues.zh: 斯多葛神情上的任何破绽，对吧？他不想让人觉得他有一丝一毫的担忧或沮丧。换句话说，毫无疑问，如果他在天有灵，

cues.en: he regrets every line he ever wrote.
cues.zh: 他会后悔写下的每一个字。

cues.en: Not because he doesn't think it might benefit us, but because it shows the sort of weakness not entirely consistent with Stoic virtue. Perhaps there are other Stoics
cues.zh: 不是因为他觉得这帮不到我们，而是因为这暴露了一种与斯多葛美德不完全相符的软弱。也许还有其他斯多葛学者

cues.en: who suffered
cues.zh: 承受了

cues.en: more pain,
cues.zh: 更多的痛苦，

cues.en: who had greater difficulties and never wrote a line. In Marcus Aurelius' view, those men would be greater than he. And Whether there exists such people or not,
cues.zh: 历经了更大的艰难，却从未写下一行字。在 Marcus Aurelius 眼中，那些人比他更伟大。而无论是否存在这样的人，

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius is a sort of standing standing reproach
cues.zh: Marcus Aurelius 都是一种恒久的鞭笞，

cues.en: to our weakness,
cues.zh: 直指我们的软弱，

cues.en: to our self indulgence,
cues.zh: 直指我们的自我放纵，

cues.en: to our willingness to give in to what we want, to our inclination to make excuses
cues.zh: 直指我们对欲望的妥协，直指我们为原本完全由自己决定的事情

cues.en: about things that were entirely up to us,
cues.zh: 找借口的倾向，

cues.en: and to try and act as if we are not responsible
cues.zh: 以及试图假装

cues.en: for our behavior.
cues.zh: 对自己的行为毫无责任。

cues.en: One might want to say that Marcus Aurelius is an important step in the construction of the Western conception of the self or the ego.
cues.zh: 有人可能会说，马可·奥勒留是西方自我或本我概念构建过程中的重要一步。

cues.en: You are the part of you, not the meat, but the will, the soul, the internal stuff. That's what you're responsible for. That's what the gods will judge you
cues.zh: 你是你自己的那部分，不是肉体，而是意志、灵魂、内在的东西。那才是你要负责的。那才是神明审判你的

cues.en: on the basis of.
cues.zh: 依据。

cues.en: Apart from that, don't worry about it. All other things are matters of indifference to you. Connect yourself to nature, do what's right, and let the devil take the hindmost. It's not your problem.
cues.zh: 除此之外，别担心。其他一切对你来说都无关紧要。与自然相连，做正确的事，让魔鬼带走落后者。那不是你的问题。

cues.en: Stoicism
cues.zh: 斯多葛主义

cues.en: is an appropriate philosophy, I would say, for
cues.zh: 我认为，是一种合适的哲学，适合

cues.en: serious, ruthless, introspective people
cues.zh: 严肃、无情、内省的人

cues.en: that want real answers and are willing to take no nonsense. In that respect, it's a kind of moral philosophy I would be inclined to teach at, say, West Point. If I were teaching people that are going to be under terrible danger and terrible fearful conditions,
cues.zh: 他们想要真正的答案，不愿接受胡说八道。在这方面，它是一种我会倾向于在比如西点军校教授的伦理哲学。如果我要教那些将身处可怕危险和恐怖条件下的人，

cues.en: I would teach them to do what they know they ought to do
cues.zh: 我会教他们去做他们知道自己应该做的事

cues.en: and to discipline and organize their emotions in such a way as they behave themselves in a way that is not disgraceful.
cues.zh: 并且以这样的方式纪律和组织他们的情绪，使他们行为得体，不做可耻之事。

cues.en: To avoid that is the epitome of Stoic virtue,
cues.zh: 避免那种情况是斯多葛美德的典范，

cues.en: and it may not have all the attractive elements of Socratic philosophy. It lacks the poetic element of Platonism.
cues.zh: 它可能没有苏格拉底哲学的所有吸引人元素。它缺乏柏拉图主义的诗意元素。

cues.en: It lacks the comprehensive
cues.zh: 它缺乏全面的

cues.en: intellectual drive
cues.zh: 知识驱动

cues.en: of Socrates,
cues.zh: 苏格拉底的，

cues.en: but it still contains elements of Stoic no... Elements of Socratic nobility
cues.zh: 但它仍然包含斯多葛的……苏格拉底高贵性的元素

cues.en: that neither skepticism
cues.zh: 既不是怀疑主义

cues.en: nor epicureanism
cues.zh: 也不是伊壁鸠鲁主义

cues.en: offer us. And in that respect, I think it's the true air of Socratic philosophy.
cues.zh: 能提供给我们的。在这方面，我认为它是苏格拉底哲学的真正气息。

cues.en: The key
cues.zh: 核心

cues.en: idea
cues.zh: 思想

cues.en: behind
cues.zh: 源于

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius is something like this:
cues.zh: 马可·奥勒留，大致是这样的：

cues.en: that it's just the human condition for us to have troubles and worries and anxieties and problems.
cues.zh: 人类遭遇烦恼、忧虑、焦虑和问题，本来就是人之常情。

cues.en: Don't
cues.zh: 不要

cues.en: torture yourself
cues.zh: 折磨自己

cues.en: by worrying about things that aren't in your control.
cues.zh: 去为那些你无法掌控的事情操心。

cues.en: Leave that in the hands of God, leave that in the hands of nature.
cues.zh: 把这些交给上帝，交给自然。

cues.en: Do your best to control the things that you do have control over: yourself, your behavior,
cues.zh: 尽你最大努力去掌控你能掌控的事情：你自己、你的行为、

cues.en: your intentions, and your actions.
cues.zh: 你的意图和你的行动。

cues.en: If you do that, you will live a blessed and happy and virtuous and wise life.
cues.zh: 如果你能做到这一点，你就会过上幸福、快乐、美德而智慧的生活。

cues.en: You will be a real human being.
cues.zh: 你将成为一个真正的人。

cues.en: If you fail to do that,
cues.zh: 如果你做不到这一点，

cues.en: gradually
cues.zh: 渐渐地，

cues.en: the inclination
cues.zh: 这种倾向

cues.en: towards
cues.zh: 朝向

cues.en: debauchery,
cues.zh: 放荡、

cues.en: evil,
cues.zh: 邪恶、

cues.en: vice,
cues.zh: 恶习、

cues.en: sin,
cues.zh: 罪孽，

cues.en: to put it in theological terms,
cues.zh: 用神学的话来说，

cues.en: will become greater and greater, and unless you unless you arrest this slide towards self indulgence,
cues.zh: 会变得越来越强烈，除非你制止这种向纵欲下滑的趋势，

cues.en: you will harm yourself, and you will harm the people around you.
cues.zh: 否则你会伤害自己，也会伤害周围的人。

cues.en: No rational being wishes to harm themselves.
cues.zh: 没有哪个理性的人愿意伤害自己。

cues.en: No rational being wishes to harm the people around them. Because of that, if we were to be rational,
cues.zh: 没有哪个理性的人愿意伤害他们周围的人。正因如此，如果我们能够保持理性，

cues.en: it is the same thing as making us good, and that is the same thing as making us free.
cues.zh: 这就等于让我们变好，这也等于让我们获得自由。

cues.en: Not free in the sense of political freedom, being a slave or a free man, but free in the sense of being autonomous,
cues.zh: 这种自由不是政治意义上的自由——即奴隶与自由人之别，而是自主意义上的自由，

cues.en: making our own decisions, making laws for ourselves.
cues.zh: 能够自己做决定，为自己立法。

cues.en: Free in the sense of no longer being a slave of our passions, being pushed about by our feelings, being a toy
cues.zh: 这种自由意味着不再做激情的奴隶，不再被情感左右，不再像一个玩具

cues.en: that gets messed with by arbitrary things that are really beneath the human condition, that are mere emotion. If we want to be fully human, we must be fully free, and that means fully rational, and that means fully good.
cues.zh: 被那些贬低人类尊严、纯属情绪化的随机事物所摆布。如果我们想成为完整的人，就必须获得完全的自由，这意味着完全理性，也意味着至善。

cues.en: Accept no substitutes, is what Marcus Aurelius says. He did that himself, and he hopes that other people will do it.
cues.zh: 接受无可替代的事物，这是马可·奥勒留说过的话。他自己践行了这一点，也希望别人能这样做。

cues.en: He did the best he could,
cues.zh: 他尽力做到了最好，

cues.en: and you can't help but feel that at the end of his life he must have felt relieved
cues.zh: 而你禁不住会想，在他生命快要结束时，他一定感到如释重负，

cues.en: that the terrible crushing burden of this loneliness, a man that has no equals and has no friends,
cues.zh: 那种可怕而沉重的孤独感，一个没有对手、没有朋友的人，

cues.en: a man that has nothing but philosophy to guide him,
cues.zh: 一个除了哲学别无所依的人，

cues.en: death must have been
cues.zh: 面对死亡，

cues.en: a great release.
cues.zh: 一定是一种巨大的解脱。

cues.en: It's like getting the evening off after you've put in your turn guarding the camp.
cues.zh: 就像在营地站完岗后，终于迎来了晚上的休息。

cues.en: And
cues.zh: 而

cues.en: instead of
cues.zh: 他没有

cues.en: becoming
cues.zh: 沦为一个

cues.en: an obscure and unimportant
cues.zh: 默默无闻、无足轻重的人，

cues.en: figure,
cues.zh: 反而

cues.en: He's become a symbol in the history of Western philosophy
cues.zh: 成为了西方哲学史上

cues.en: of
cues.zh: 象征

cues.en: the practical,
cues.zh: 务实、

cues.en: concrete,
cues.zh: 具体、

cues.en: immediate virtues.
cues.zh: 切近的美德的化身。

cues.en: The sort of virtues which are accessible to us, not because we have profound intellectual ability, not because we're a Newton or a Kant, but simply because we have problems, and we're everyday rational human beings.
cues.zh: 这种美德是我们都能企及的，不是因为我们有多深厚的智力，不是因为我们是牛顿或康德，而仅仅是因为我们面临问题，我们是拥有日常理性的普通人。

cues.en: The stoic man says that a virtue that is possible for one man is accessible to all of us. There is no excuse for us not being that good. If we provide such excuses for ourselves, we harm ourselves and we harm others by preventing us from recognizing our true moral obligations.
cues.zh: 斯多葛学派认为，一个人能做到的美德，我们所有人也都能做到。我们没有理由不去做到那么好。如果我们为自己找这种借口，就是在伤害自己，也通过阻止我们认清真正的道德义务而伤害了他人。

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius lets us know
cues.zh: 马可·奥勒留让我们明白，

cues.en: that all people suffer,
cues.zh: 所有人都在承受苦难，

cues.en: but that not all people pity themselves.
cues.zh: 但并不是所有人都在顾影自怜。

cues.en: Marcus Aurelius lets us know
cues.zh: 马可·奥勒留让我们明白，

cues.en: that all men die,
cues.zh: 所有人终将一死，

cues.en: but that not all men die whining.
cues.zh: 但并不是所有人都死得满腹牢骚。

cues.en: Something to think about, take home with you and mull it over.
cues.zh: 有些事值得你思考，带回去细细琢磨。
